encounters.cc: progressive tightening of the skin on her hands and face

lines: Progressive tightening of the skin on her hands and face
A 45-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of progressive tightening of the skin on her hands and face.
She reports that her fingers become white and painful when exposed to cold temperatures.
She also mentions difficulty swallowing, especially solid foods, and has had episodes of heartburn.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
Smoking: Current smoker, 2 packs per day for 20 years.
On physical examination, you note thickened skin on her fingers extending proximally to the metacarpophalangeal joints and facial skin that appears shiny and taut with loss of expression lines.
Pulmonary function tests show a reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO).

encounters.cc: progressive dry mouth and difficulty swallowing dry foods, gritty sensation in her eyes

lines: Progressive dry mouth and difficulty swallowing dry foods, gritty sensation in her eyes

A 52-year-old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and systemic sclerosis diagnosed in January returns to the Rheumatology clinic with a 6-month history of progressive dry mouth and difficulty swallowing dry foods.
She also reports a gritty sensation in her eyes and has needed to use artificial tears multiple times a day.
She has a past medical history of hypothyroidism and rheumatoid arthritis.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
Smoking: Current smoker, 2 packs per day for 20 years.
On physical examination, you note dry oral mucosa and dental caries.
Her Schirmer test shows decreased lacrimation with less than 5 mm of wetting after 5 minutes.
Her parotid glands are mildly enlarged and non-tender.

encounters.cc: increasing fatigue, difficulty climbing stairs, and a rash on her face and hands

lines: Increasing fatigue, difficulty climbing stairs, and a rash on her face and hands
The patient returns to the rheumatology clinic for follow-up of systemic sclerosis and autoimmune sialadenitis.
She presents with a 3-month history of increasing fatigue, difficulty climbing stairs, and a rash on her face and hands.
She reports that the rash worsens with sun exposure.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
Smoking: Current smoker, 2 packs per day for 20 years.
On physical examination, you note a heliotrope rash with periorbital edema and erythematous, scaly plaques over the knuckles, known as Gottron's papules.
Muscle strength testing reveals symmetrical proximal muscle weakness.

encounters.cc: morning stiffness in her hands and symmetrical joint pain

lines: Morning stiffness in her hands and symmetrical joint pain

The patient is a 55-year-old female with rheumatoid arthritis, systemic sclerosis, and prior autoimmune sialadenitis and dermatomyositis who presents to the emergency department with a 6-month history of morning stiffness in her hands that lasts for more than an hour and symmetrical joint pain.
She reports that her symptoms improve with activity.
She also complains of recent onset neck pain and occasional numbness in her extremities.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
Smoking: Current smoker, 2 packs per day for 20 years.
On physical examination, there is noticeable swelling and tenderness over her metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints.
There is also a limited range of motion in her cervical spine.
Radiographs of her hands show periarticular osteopenia and marginal erosions.
The patient returns after January ED visit and presents to the clinic with complaints of muscle weakness and fatigue for the past two weeks.
- Atlantoaxial subluxation secondary to rheumatoid arthritis (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
She has a history of hypertension.
She takes which is currently managed with hydrochlorothiazide.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
Smoking: Current smoker, 2 packs per day for 20 years.
She denies any headaches, palpitations, or excessive sweating.
Physical examination is unremarkable except for mild muscle tenderness.

encounters.cc: 2-week history of insomnia, tremors, and palpitations

lines: 2-week history of insomnia, tremors, and palpitations
The patient with systemic sclerosis, dermatomyositis, and atlantoaxial subluxation presents with insomnia, tremors, and palpitations.
Her asthma was well-controlled with inhaled corticosteroids and a leukotriene receptor antagonist.
A month ago, she experienced an asthma exacerbation, after which her physician added slow-release theophylline.
- Atlantoaxial subluxation secondary to rheumatoid arthritis (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Secondary Hyperaldosteronism due to Dietary Sodium Restriction (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
Medical history is notable for hypertension, gastroesophageal reflux disease and rheumatoid arthritis.
Current medications include albuterol, lisinopril, cimetidine, methotrexate and occasional aspirin.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
Smoking: Current smoker, 2 packs per day for 20 years.
She denies fever, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

encounters.cc: spontaneous bloody discharge from her right nipple

lines: Spontaneous bloody discharge from her right nipple

The patient is a 56-year-old female with established rheumatoid arthritis, systemic sclerosis, and dermatomyositis who presents to the clinic with a three-month history of spontaneous bloody discharge from her right nipple.
She also reports a palpable mass in her right breast that she discovered one month ago.
She denies any fever, weight loss, or changes in skin over the breast.
- Atlantoaxial subluxation secondary to rheumatoid arthritis (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Secondary Hyperaldosteronism due to Dietary Sodium Restriction (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
She has no family history of breast cancer.
Smoking: Current smoker, 2 packs per day for 20 years.
On physical examination, a 2 cm firm, non-tender mass is palpated in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast.
Mammography shows a 2 cm irregular mass with speculated margins in the right breast.
Ultrasound confirms a solid mass with irregular borders and increased vascularity.

The patient is a 57-year-old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis, systemic sclerosis, dermatomyositis, and recently diagnosed invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast who is brought to the emergency department by her coworker after suddenly developing an excruciating headache.
She had just finished a long day at the office and was climbing the stairs to the parking lot when she felt a sudden "explosion" inside her head, causing her to fall against the railing.

She describes the pain as unlike anything she has ever experienced, calling it the "worst headache of her life." She remembers feeling nauseated immediately after the onset and briefly closing her eyes because the pain was so intense.
She does not recall losing consciousness.
Since the onset of pain, she has experienced persistent throbbing in her head, worsened by movement and light exposure.
She reports blurry vision and double vision, particularly when trying to look to the right.
She has also noticed difficulty keeping her left eye open, which her coworker confirms appeared droopy during the car ride to the hospital.
She denies prior episodes of similar headache, recent illness, or head trauma.
- Atlantoaxial subluxation secondary to rheumatoid arthritis (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Secondary Hyperaldosteronism due to Dietary Sodium Restriction (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
- Invasive ductal carcinoma of right breast (diagnosed 2024-07-15)
Her medical history is notable for 15 years of hypertension.
She takes for which she takes atenolol.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
She has no known family history of aneurysms or connective tissue disorders, though her mother died suddenly of a stroke at age 60.
She has smoked two packs of cigarettes daily for the past 20 years but denies alcohol or illicit drug use.
She has not had regular health checkups in several years.
Her vital signs show a blood pressure of 152/88 mm Hg, pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 16/min, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air.
On arrival, she appears in moderate distress, holding her head and shielding her eyes from the bright overhead lights.
On general inspection, she is alert and oriented but repeatedly asks the nurse to dim the lights.
Neurologic examination shows left-sided ptosis, with the left eyelid drooping significantly compared to the right.
The left pupil is 6.5 mm and sluggishly reactive to light, whereas the right pupil is 4.5 mm and briskly reactive.
Upward gaze and adduction of the left eye are limited, while abduction remains intact.
The right eye moves normally in all directions.
When asked to look to the right, she complains of double vision.
Facial sensation is intact, speech is fluent, and motor strength is normal in all extremities.
Sensory testing is unremarkable, and reflexes are symmetric.
Cardiac exam reveals a regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable.
A noncontrast CT scan of the head is shown.
